R01.text: Your first week matched your 28-day baseline well: sleep ~475 min starting ~22:45–22:55, ending 07:00, with stable steps (~8,000) and HRV (~45 ms). From Apr 7 onward, sleep start shifted markedly later (around 00:08–00:15), reducing sleep to ~385–392 min while wake time remained fixed at 07:00. Nighttime coverage dropped to ~405–412 min during these six nights, so some sleep may be unrecorded. Activity minutes alternated between 45 and 90 min (baseline 50–60), often in evening blocks. Resting heart rate and HRV remained near baseline despite the schedule shift.

R02.text: In your 14-day window, sleep timing shifted on 7 nights: starts moved from ~22:50 to after midnight, reducing duration to ~385-392 min while wake time stayed at 07:00. On other nights, sleep remained ~474-485 min. Activity alternated between 45 and 90 min versus a steady ~56-min baseline. Steps (~8,088), RHR (~56 bpm), and RMSSD (~46 ms) stayed near baseline.

R03.text: Your first week matched your 28-day baseline well: sleep ~470–485 min (22:35–07:00), steps ~7600–8300, HRV ~43–47 ms, and RHR ~56 bpm. From Apr 7 onward, sleep start times shifted later (around midnight) and recorded sleep duration dropped to ~385–392 min for six consecutive nights, with nighttime coverage falling to ~405–412 min from ~490+. Steps (~8000–8400), active minutes, RHR, and HRV remained at baseline levels throughout. Because daytime wear stayed complete while nighttime coverage decreased alongside shorter recorded sleep, the reduced sleep values may partly reflect less overnight device recording rather than only a true sleep change. Consider checking device fit or charging habits at night.

In the 14-day window, activity alternated between 45 and 90 min. From Apr 7, sleep start shifted to ~00:10, reducing duration to ~389 min on those nights while steps (~8088) and RMSSD stayed stable.

R08.text: Across 28 baseline days, sleep averaged 471 min (start ~22:50, end fixed 07:00), steps ~7947, activity ~56 min, RHR 55.9 bpm, RMSSD 45.0 ms. In the 14-day window, activity alternated strictly between 90 and 45 min (mean 64.3 vs 55.6 baseline). Sleep split into two phases: days 1–6 maintained ~479 min, then days 7–14 abruptly shortened to ~385–392 min with starts shifting to ~00:08–00:15 and reduced nighttime coverage (~405–412 min vs ~490 baseline). Steps (~8088), RHR, and RMSSD remained stable throughout.

R09.text: During the 28-day baseline, sleep averaged 471 min starting ~22:50 and ending at 07:00, steps ~7947, activity ~56 min, RHR 56 bpm, RMSSD 45 ms. The 14-day window showed two distinct phases. Days 1-6 maintained baseline patterns but activity alternated between 45 and 90 min. From day 7 onward, sleep start shifted abruptly past midnight (~00:08-00:15), reducing sleep duration to 385-392 min (mean window 441 vs 471 baseline). Nighttime coverage dropped to ~405-412 min during this phase. Steps, RHR, and RMSSD remained stable throughout. Activity continued alternating 45/90 min. The late sleep onset persisted through day 14 without recovery.
